title: connect: bound post-connect blocking connects by their own start
body:
Supersedes #23506.

This PR has two commits: the fix and the test.

## Problem

curl drops the connect timeout when a transfer reaches MSTATE_DO. A
blocking connect can then wait forever. The TLS handshake of an FTPS
data connection is one example.

The original patch in #23506 stops the hang. But it starts the timer
when the blocking wait starts. `CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT.md` says the
connection phase includes the name resolve and all protocol handshakes
until the connection is established. For a passive FTPS data connection,
the TCP connect and the wait for the 150 response happen before the
blocking wait. The original patch does not count them.

## Change

- Record when `Curl_conn_connect()` first sees each socket.
- Use that time for the blocking connect timeout after `MSTATE_DO`.
- Clear the time when the socket's filter chain is discarded. A new
  data connection then gets a new timeout.
- Move the connect timeout default and the expired timeout rule into
  one helper. `timeleft_now_ms()` uses the same helper.

## Test

`STALLDATA` is a new mode in the FTP test server. It accepts the data
connection and sends no data. Test 1792 waits one second before the 150
response. Then the data TLS handshake stalls.

~~The test uses `--max-time 5` as a safety bound. A postcheck reads
`time_total`. It fails when the value is 2.8 seconds or more. This
rejects a total-timeout exit and a timer that starts after the 150
response.~~

The test uses `--max-time 5` as a safety bound. A postcheck reads
`time_total` and `time_appconnect`, subtracts the control connection
setup, and fails when the remaining time is 2.8 seconds or more. This
rejects a total-timeout exit and a timer that starts after the 150
response, without counting a slow control connection.

## Results

| Binary | time_total | result |
|---|---|---|
| this branch | 2.017s | pass |
| #23506 | 3.018s | fail |
| master | 5.000s | fail |

FTP/FTPS tests 400, 401, 402, 405, 1112, 1790, and 1792 pass.

## Credit

The original patch is by @1rhino2 in #23506.

## Open question

Should the timer start at the first `Curl_conn_connect()` call for the
socket? That call covers the DNS, TCP, and handshake work in the filter
chain. It does not cover FTP setup before that call. A protocol-level
timestamp is needed for an earlier start.

   test1488.pl \

+  test1792.pl \
   test3990.pl
 
 EXTRA_DIST =         \

@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="US-ASCII"?>
+<testcase>
+<info>
+<keywords>
+FTP
+FTPS
+EPSV
+RETR
+timeout
+STALLDATA
+timing-dependent
+</keywords>
+</info>
+
+# Server-side
+<reply>
+<servercmd>
+DELAY RETR 1
+STALLDATA
+REPLY "PBSZ 0" 200 OK
+REPLY "PROT P" 200 OK
+</servercmd>
+<data nocheck="yes">
+data
+</data>
+</reply>
+
+# Client-side
+<client>
+<features>
+SSL
+</features>
+<server>
+ftps
+</server>
+<killserver>
+ftps
+</killserver>
+<name>
+FTPS data connection connect timeout includes the 150 wait
+</name>
+<command>
+--insecure --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 5 --write-out '%{time_total} %{time_appconnect}' ftps://%HOSTIP:%FTPSPORT/%TESTNUMBER
+</command>
+</client>
+
+# Verify data after the test has been "shot"
+<verify>
+# 28 is CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT
+<errorcode>
+28
+</errorcode>
+<protocol crlf="yes">
+USER anonymous
+PASS ftp@example.com
+PBSZ 0
+PROT P
+PWD
+EPSV
+TYPE I
+SIZE %TESTNUMBER
+RETR %TESTNUMBER
+</protocol>
+# The 150 wait and the stalled handshake must both count. The postcheck
+# subtracts time_appconnect, so the control connection setup does not count.
+# The fix ends the wait at the 2 second connect timeout; a total-timeout
+# exit, or a timer started after the 150 response, takes 3 seconds or more
+# and fails.
+<postcheck>
+%PERL %SRCDIR/test1792.pl %LOGDIR/stdout%TESTNUMBER
+</postcheck>
+</verify>
+</testcase>

+###########################################################################
+#
+# Verify that test 1792 stopped at the connect timeout, not at the total
+# timeout. The first line of the file holds the time_total and time_appconnect
+# values written by curl. Subtract the control connection setup so a slow
+# runner does not count it against the connect timeout.
+#
+use strict;
+use warnings;
+
+use constant LIMIT_SECONDS => 2.8;
+
+my $file = shift @ARGV;
+open(my $fh, "<", $file) or exit 1;
+my $line = <$fh>;
+close($fh);
+$line = '' unless(defined $line);
+my ($total, $appconnect) = split(' ', $line);
+exit 1 unless(defined $appconnect);
+my $elapsed = ($total + 0) - ($appconnect + 0);
+exit($elapsed >= LIMIT_SECONDS);
